task.description: Implement the validated ISS-0226 design (PASS, step-05, commit 11f587d): give Letflow.SandboxPool's worker result a closed type, make handle_info/2's clause A total over that type, and add regression tests driving the previously-unhandled shape.
acceptance_criteria: The worker result has an explicit closed type (struct or tagged tuple set) declared in lib/letflow/sandbox_pool.ex
handle_info/2 is total over that type -- an unrecognised shape is handled, not a function-clause crash
A test drives an unexpected run_op/1 return and asserts the pool survives with slot bookkeeping intact
No change to the ISS-0224 invariants INV-SP-A1..A3 or the owner-monitor reclaim semantics

result.summary: Implemented lib/letflow/design/iss0226-sandbox-pool-worker-result-typing.md verbatim, no deviations. In lib/letflow/sandbox_pool.ex: added `require Logger`; added @typep provision_result/drop_result/worker_result (§3.1, byte-for-byte the union the design specified); added @spec to the existing run_op/1 (body unchanged); added a new private, total `classify_worker_result/2` (chosen name -- matches the design's suggested name exactly) with the four legal (op-kind, result) clauses plus a catch-all returning :invalid; added op_kind/1 and op_sandbox_id/1 accessors (design §6, chosen names match the design exactly) mirroring the existing op_schema_name/1 idiom. Rewrote only the `else` branch body of handle_info({ref, result}, state) when is_reference(ref): demonitor still runs first and unconditionally (ordering preserved verbatim per §4.2), then classify_worker_result/2 is called; {:ok, validated_result} runs the unchanged complete_op/3 |> service_next_waiter/1 |> pump/1 pipeline; :invalid logs via Logger.error/1 (op kind, sandbox id, inspect(result)) and runs handle_worker_death/1 |> service_next_waiter/1 |> pump/1 instead. complete_op/3, handle_worker_death/1, clause B, state shape, and all public @specs are untouched (confirmed via the diff, matching §2.2/§4.3's scope boundary). `mix compile --warnings-as-errors`: clean, no warnings. Added two tests to test/letflow/sandbox_pool_test.exs's new describe block 'handle_info/2 survives an unrecognized worker result (ISS-0226 regression, acceptance criterion 3)': (1) primary case, :sys.replace_state/2 injects a well-formed {:provision, _} in_flight entry with a fabricated task_ref, send(pool, {fake_ref, :not_a_recognized_shape}) drives the :invalid path; asserts Process.alive?(pool), waits (via the file's existing wait_until_pool_state/pool_drained? idiom) for in_flight to recover to nil, asserts the pool's own mailbox is empty, and asserts a subsequent claim/2+release/2 round-trip still works. (2) companion case per design §7.2, same mechanism against an injected {:drop, purpose: :release} op with a real reply tag, asserting the blocked caller receives {:error, :release_failed} in addition to the same survive/recover assertions. `mix test test/letflow/sandbox_pool_test.exs`: Result: 18 passed, 0 failed (16 pre-existing + 2 new; ran to completion synchronously, real Postgres, no mocks). Deviations from design: none -- implementation matches §3/§4.2/§5/§6/§7 exactly; chosen function/type names are exactly those the design proposed. INV-SP-A1..A3 and owner-monitor reclaim semantics: unaffected -- complete_op/3, handle_worker_death/1, clause B, state shape, and reserve_slot/2 bodies are byte-for-byte unchanged (verified via git diff), matching the design's §8 checklist. This is not a new tenant-data path (no new API route, no migration, no secrets, no response-shaping change) -- it is a defensive-programming fix inside an already-designed internal GenServer callback, so SECURITY-REVIEWER is not obviously required by the security-invariants.md tenant-data-path criterion; however the change touches the crash-recovery path of a supervised process holding all slot bookkeeping, so REVIEWER's OTP-idiom/supervision-integrity gate is squarely in scope and the required next step.
result.next_action: Route to REVIEWER (OTP idiom / supervision-integrity gate). ORCH's call whether SECURITY-REVIEWER also gates this -- this ELIXIR-DEV run assessed it as not tenant-data-path but flags the question rather than deciding it unilaterally.
